+# Behavior docs must change together with user-visible behavior.
+vars:
+  source_paths: ["src/**"]
+  docs_paths: ["docs/**"]
+  error_type_paths: ["**/errors.ts"]
+
+rules:
+  - id: docs.behavior-change-without-docs
+    description: User-visible behavior changed without a docs update
+    type: noul
+    scope: pr
+    locate: false
+    severity: minor
+    when: { files_changed: ["{{vars.source_paths}}"], files_unchanged: ["{{vars.docs_paths}}"] }
+    instructions: >-
+      Using `pr` and `files`, does this pull request change user-visible behavior of the app,
+      such as new or changed UI, workflows, defaults, settings, keyboard shortcuts or error
+      messages? `stats` and `files` list what changed; no documentation file
+      ({{vars.docs_paths}}) was changed.
+    criteria:
+      true: The title or description describes a new feature or changed behavior users will notice.
+      false: Internal refactor, tests, build or CI changes, dependency updates, or a fix that restores documented behavior.
+  - id: docs.new-ipc-without-docs
+    description: New IPC handler without a docs update
+    type: pattern
+    field: added_lines
+    fires_when: match
+    severity: minor
+    paths: ["{{vars.source_paths}}"]
+    regex: '\bipcMain\.handle\(\s*[''"]'
+    when: { files_unchanged: ["{{vars.docs_paths}}"] }

+# Checks on the pull request title and description. Findings appear in the summary comment.
+# Exact formats (ticket id pattern, Conventional Commits prefix) are better checked with a regex in CI;
+# these rules cover what needs reading: is the title specific, does the description explain why.
+context:
+  include_pr_body: true
+
+rules:
+  - id: pr.title-specific
+    description: Title does not say what the change does
+    type: noul
+    scope: pr
+    severity: minor
+    locate: false
+    fires_on: "no"
+    instructions: >-
+      Ignoring markers such as WIP, Draft or DO NOT MERGE, does `pr.title` say what the change
+      does and which part of the system it affects, specifically enough that a teammate could
+      tell what changed without opening the pull request?
+    criteria:
+      true: 'Specific titles such as "Add CSV export to the invoices list", "WIP: payment retries with backoff" or "Fix token refresh race in the auth client".'
+      false: Generic or empty titles such as "Fix bug", "Updates", "Changes", "Small fixes", a bare ticket number or a branch name like "feature/user-search".
+
+  - id: pr.title-unfinished
+    description: Title marks the change as unfinished
+    type: noul
+    scope: pr
+    severity: major
+    locate: false
+    instructions: >-
+      Does `pr.title` mark the change as unfinished or not ready to merge, for example with WIP,
+      DO NOT MERGE, DNM, draft, temp or "not ready"?

+# Svelte 5 runes.
+vars:
+  svelte_paths: ["**/*.svelte", "**/*.svelte.ts"]
+  svelte_component_paths: ["**/*.svelte"]
+  max_component_lines: "300"
+  # Optional: calls that only read state, so an effect made of them is still a derivation.
+  # pure_reads: "Calls to get*() store getters only read state."
+
+rules:
+  - id: svelte.effect-without-cleanup
+    description: $effect starts a listener, timer, subscription or observer without returning a cleanup
+    type: noul
+    severity: major
+    paths: ["{{vars.svelte_paths}}"]
+    instructions: >-
+      Is there an added Svelte `$effect(() => { ... })` block in `changes.lines` whose body
+      starts something that keeps running (addEventListener, setInterval, setTimeout, a
+      subscribe or on* subscription, or a ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver or
+      MutationObserver), and whose body does not return a function that removes, clears,
+      unsubscribes or disconnects it?
+    criteria:
+      true: Inside the $effect body a listener, timer, subscription or observer is created and the effect has no return statement that undoes it.
+      false: >-
+        No $effect is added, the $effect only reads or assigns state, or it returns a cleanup:
+        a function (return () => ...), a variable holding the unsubscribe function
+        (return unsub), or the result of the subscribe call itself
+        (return window.api.onSomething(...), which returns its unsubscribe function).
+        Timers and listeners outside $effect do not count.
+  - id: svelte.legacy-export-let
+    description: Legacy `export let` prop; use $props() with an interface
+    type: pattern
